title: 12  QUESTION-MODULE-SPEC
text:
12.8 Tests and test flow

Tests config (src/lib/tests-config.ts) uses questionIds (logical_ids). When a test is started, the client receives these ids and fetches each via GET /api/questions/[id], which returns the latest version (from DB) for that logical_id. On submit, the client sends questionId and version per answer so the server grades the same version the student saw and stores it in answers.question_id and answers.question_version.

title: 8  SPEC-QUESTION-COLLECTIONS-0.0.2.qmd
text:
9 Question Collections — SPEC 0.0.2
This spec defines question collections: named sets of questions that can be used as a test, a homework assignment, or a study list. It extends the MVP (SPEC-0.0.1) by adding UI and persistence for creating and managing collections, and clarifies terminology so that “test” is reserved for the activity of taking and submitting answers, not for the underlying set of questions.
References: SPEC-0.0.1.qmd, PRD-0.0.1-v003.qmd, QUESTION-FORMAT-0.0.1.qmd, QUESTION-MODULE-SPEC.qmd.
See DOC-GUIDE-v001.qmd for document versioning.

title: 8  SPEC-QUESTION-COLLECTIONS-0.0.2.qmd
text:
9.1 Purpose and scope

9.1.1 What is a question collection?
A question collection (or collection) is a named, ordered list of question identifiers. The same collection can be used in different ways:

As a test — A learner takes the collection under timed/untimed conditions, submits answers, and receives a score. This is the current “take a test” flow.
As homework — The same set of questions might be assigned as homework (same or different submission rules in a future version).
As a study list — A topic-focused set of questions for practice, with or without grading.

The system does not assume every collection is a “test.” Naming and UI should reflect that collections are generic question sets; the use of a collection (e.g. “Take as test”) is a separate action.


9.1.2 Naming: “Collection” vs “Test”







Term
Meaning in this spec




Question collection
A named set of questions (data). Can be used as a test, homework, or study list.


Test
The activity of taking a collection: start session, answer questions, submit, get score. “Test” = one usage of a collection.


Test session
One user attempt (e.g. one “take” of a collection). Already in DB as test_sessions.



So: collections are the reusable question sets; tests (and test sessions) are the act of taking and submitting. The UI and docs should avoid implying that every collection is “a test”; prefer “collection” for the entity and “Take as test” (or similar) for the action.


9.1.3 Scope for 0.0.2

In scope

Persist question collections in the database (new table and APIs).
UI to create a new collection: choose a name (and optional description) and select which questions to include (from available questions).
UI to list collections; from the list, the user can take a collection as a test (existing take flow) or later edit/delete (optional for 0.0.2).
Replace or refactor the current config-based “tests” (tests-config.ts, TESTS_CONFIG env) so that collections are the source of truth; “take test” uses a collection id.
Update documentation and code naming so that “collection” is used for the set of questions and “test” is used for the taking/submission flow where appropriate.

Out of scope for 0.0.2

Editing or deleting collections (can be added later).
Different “modes” per collection (e.g. homework vs test); for now, every collection can be “taken as a test.”
Ordering of questions within a collection (fixed order or shuffle) is MVP-defined; spec allows storing order.

title: 8  SPEC-QUESTION-COLLECTIONS-0.0.2.qmd
text:
9.2 Data model

9.2.1 New table: question_collections
Store one row per collection.








Column
Type
Description




id
uuid, PK
Unique collection id (e.g. gen_random_uuid()).


title
text, not null
User-facing name (e.g. “Bash basics”, “Week 3 homework”).


description
text, nullable
Optional description.


owner_id
uuid, nullable, FK → auth.users
User who created the collection. Nullable to allow system/seed data.


created_at
timestamptz
When the collection was created.





9.2.2 New table: question_collection_items
Store the questions in each collection with explicit order.








Column
Type
Description




id
uuid, PK
Unique row id.


collection_id
uuid, not null, FK → question_collections(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
Which collection.


question_logical_id
text, not null
Question logical id (same as in question_versions / storage).


position
int, not null
1-based order within the collection.



Unique constraint on (collection_id, position) or (collection_id, question_logical_id) depending on whether the same question can appear more than once; for 0.0.2, one question per collection is sufficient, so unique on (collection_id, question_logical_id) is acceptable. Order is given by position.


9.2.3 Relationship to existing tables

test_sessions: Keep test_id but treat it as collection_id (uuid). So “test_id” in test_sessions is semantically “the collection id used for this test.” Migrations can rename the column to collection_id for clarity, or keep the name and document that it refers to a collection; either way, the value is the uuid from question_collections.id.
answers: No change; they reference session_id and store question_id / question_version.



9.2.4 RLS (row-level security)

question_collections: Authenticated users can read all collections (so everyone can “take” any collection). Insert: authenticated users can create (set owner_id = self). Update/delete: only owner (or later, admin) if you add edit/delete in 0.0.2.
question_collection_items: Same as collections: read for authenticated; insert/update/delete only when the user owns the parent collection (or via policy that checks question_collections.owner_id).

title: 8  SPEC-QUESTION-COLLECTIONS-0.0.2.qmd
text:
9.3 API

9.3.1 Collections








Method / path
Auth
Purpose




GET /api/collections
Authenticated
List all collections (id, title, description, question count). Optional: filter by owner.


GET /api/collections/[id]
Authenticated
Get one collection by id with ordered list of question logical ids (for “take as test” flow).


POST /api/collections
Authenticated
Create collection. Body: { title: string, description?: string, questionLogicalIds: string[] }. Returns { id, title, ... }.



For 0.0.2, no PATCH/DELETE is required; they can be added in a later spec.


9.3.2 Backward compatibility with “take test” flow

Start test: POST /api/tests/[id]/start — id is now a collection id (uuid). Server loads collection by id, gets ordered question_logical_id list, creates a test_session with test_id = collection_id (or renames to collection_id), returns sessionId, questionIds, etc. Same contract as today.
Submit test: POST /api/tests/[id]/submit — unchanged; id is still the collection id used for this test.
List “tests” for the learner: GET /api/tests can be replaced by GET /api/collections (or both supported, with /api/tests returning collections so the take-test UI keeps working). Prefer a single source: list collections, and the “Take as test” action uses the collection id.

So: the existing take-test API paths can remain under /api/tests/ for backward compatibility, but they operate on collection ids; the tests list page should be driven by collections.

title: 8  SPEC-QUESTION-COLLECTIONS-0.0.2.qmd
text:

10.4 Frontend — Question creation and management

Create/upload new questions: Any authenticated user can create questions (form or file upload). Server validates per QUESTION-FORMAT-0.0.1.qmd. If validation fails, upload is rejected with clear errors; if it passes, the question is stored and the version is approved (uploader is owner).

14 Question Sets — SPEC 0.0.2
This spec defines question sets: named, ordered lists of questions that can be used as a test, a homework assignment, or a study list. It extends the MVP (SPEC-0.0.1) by adding UI and persistence for creating and managing question sets, and clarifies terminology so that “test” is reserved for the activity of taking and submitting answers, not for the underlying set of questions.
References: SPEC-0.0.1.qmd, PRD-0.0.1-v003.qmd, QUESTION-FORMAT-0.0.1.qmd, QUESTION-MODULE-SPEC.qmd, QUESTION-SET-FORMAT-0.0.2.qmd.
See DOC-GUIDE-v001.qmd for document versioning.

title: 13  SPEC-QUESTION-SETS-0.0.2.qmd
text:
14.1 Purpose and scope

14.1.1 What is a question set?
A question set is a named, ordered list of question identifiers. The same question set can be used in different ways:

As a test — A learner takes the set under timed/untimed conditions, submits answers, and receives a score. This is the “take as test” flow.
As homework — The same set of questions might be assigned as homework (same or different submission rules in a future version).
As a study list — A topic-focused set of questions for practice, with or without grading.

The system does not assume every question set is a “test.” Naming and UI should reflect that question sets are generic; the use of a set (e.g. “Take as test”) is a separate action.


14.1.2 Naming: “Question set” vs “Test”







Term
Meaning in this spec




Question set
A named set of questions (data). Can be used as a test, homework, or study list.


Test
The activity of taking a question set: start session, answer questions, submit, get score. “Test” = one usage of a question set.


Test session
One user attempt (e.g. one “take” of a question set). Stored in DB as test_sessions.



So: question sets are the reusable data; tests (and test sessions) are the act of taking and submitting. The UI and docs should avoid implying that every question set is “a test”; prefer “question set” for the entity and “Take as test” (or similar) for the action.


14.1.3 Scope for 0.0.2

In scope

Persist question sets in the database (new tables and APIs).
UI to create a new question set: choose a name (and optional description) and select which questions to include (from available questions).
UI to list question sets; from the list, the user can take a set as a test (take flow) or later edit/delete (optional for 0.0.2).
Remove the config-based “tests” (tests-config.ts, TESTS_CONFIG env). Question sets are stored in the database (source of truth). The filesystem under question-sets/ is imported via sync only (same model as questions). See QUESTION-SET-FORMAT-0.0.2.qmd for the file layout; sync upserts into question_sets with source_slug set to the folder name.
Update documentation and code naming so that “question set” is used for the set of questions and “test” is used only for the taking/submission flow.

Out of scope for 0.0.2

Editing or deleting question sets (can be added later).
Different “modes” per set (e.g. homework vs test); for now, every question set can be “taken as a test.”
Ordering of questions within a set (fixed order or shuffle) is MVP-defined; spec allows storing order.

Column
Type
Description

text, nullable, unique when present

Store the questions in each question set with explicit order.








Column
Type
Description

uuid, PK
Unique row id.

uuid, not null, FK → question_sets(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
Which question set.

text, not null

int, not null

Unique constraint on (question_set_id, question_logical_id) so the same question appears at most once per set. Order is given by position.


14.2.3 Sources of question set data

Database (source of truth): Tables question_sets and question_set_items. Listing, get-by-id, and take flow use the DB only. Optional column source_slug identifies sets imported from a repo folder.
Filesystem (import only): Per QUESTION-SET-FORMAT-0.0.2.qmd, one folder per set with set.yaml. Sync (startup and POST /api/admin/sync-questions) reads these folders and upserts into the DB—same approach as question sync. There is no runtime merge of DB + filesystem lists.

14.2.5 RLS (row-level security)

question_sets: Authenticated users can read all question sets (so everyone can “take as test” any set). Insert: authenticated users can create (set owner_id = self). Update/delete: only owner (or later, admin) when edit/delete is added.
question_set_items: Read for authenticated; insert/update/delete only when the user owns the parent question set (policy checks question_sets.owner_id).

Each question set has its own folder under a configured root (e.g. question-sets/).
Layout: {root}/{set_id}/ where set_id is a unique identifier (e.g. UUID or slug such as bash-basics). The set_id MUST match the id field in the set file (see below).

text:
22.2 Required file: set.yaml
Each question set folder MUST contain a file named set.yaml. This file holds the set identity, title, optional description, and the ordered list of question logical ids.

22.2.1 Required fields



Field
Type
Description




id
string
Unique question set id. MUST match the parent folder name (the set_id in the path). Use a UUID or a stable slug (e.g. bash-basics, week-3-homework).


title
string
User-facing name for the set (e.g. “Bash basics”, “Week 3 homework”).


question_logical_ids
array of strings
Ordered list of question logical ids (as in QUESTION-FORMAT-0.0.1.qmd). Order in the array is the order questions are presented when the set is taken as a test. Each element MUST be a non-empty string; duplicates are allowed in the format but the system MAY normalize to unique ids per set.





22.2.2 Optional fields








Field
Type
Description




description
string
Short description of the set (e.g. for the list UI).


instructions
string
Instructions shown to the user when taking the set (e.g. how to use attached files).


attached_files
array of objects
Optional list of files that may be used to answer questions. Each object has filename (string, required) and description (string, optional). Files are stored in a files/ subfolder under the set folder.


sandbox_zip_ref
string
Filename or path to a zip containing a shared sandbox folder tree for bash (Type A) questions in this set. When present, it can be used as the default for questions that do not define their own sandbox_zip_ref.


created_at
string
ISO 8601 date (user or system).


modified_at
string

text:
22.4 Validation rules
Implementations that read or validate file-based question sets MUST enforce:

Path and id: The parent folder name MUST equal the id value in set.yaml. If they differ, the set is invalid (reject or report an error).
Required fields: id, title, and question_logical_ids MUST be present. question_logical_ids MUST be an array; it MAY be empty (empty set).
Types: id and title MUST be non-empty strings. Each element of question_logical_ids MUST be a non-empty string.
No extra structure: Unknown top-level keys MAY be ignored or preserved for forward compatibility; they MUST NOT cause validation to fail.

text:
22.5 Relationship to questions

Each value in question_logical_ids refers to a question by its logical id (the same id used in the question folder path under the questions root, e.g. questions/{logical_id}/{version}/). The system that uses the set (e.g. when taking as a test) resolves each logical id to a concrete question version (e.g. latest approved) per QUESTION-MODULE-SPEC.qmd and SPEC-0.0.1.qmd.
References to non-existent questions do not invalidate the set file; at runtime, the loader MAY skip missing questions or fail depending on implementation.

title: 13  QUESTION-MODULE-SPEC
text:
13.8 Question sets and take-as-test flow

Question sets are defined in the database and/or on the filesystem (see SPEC-QUESTION-SETS-0.0.2.qmd and QUESTION-SET-FORMAT-0.0.2.qmd). When a user takes a set as a test, the client calls POST /api/question-sets/[id]/start, receives questionIds (logical_ids), and fetches each via GET /api/questions/[id], which returns the latest approved version (from DB) for that logical_id. On submit, the client sends questionId and version per answer so the server grades the same version the student saw and stores it in answers.question_id and answers.question_version. Test sessions store set_id (uuid) referencing question_sets.id.

title: 21  QUESTION-FORMAT-0.0.1.qmd”
text:
21.6 Optional: db_meta.yaml (app metadata)
When the system writes or syncs question versions to the filesystem, it may add a separate file db_meta.yaml in each version folder. This file is optional and app-specific. It contains only: owner_id (uuid), status (approved or pending), proposed_by (uuid or null). It is used for DB–FS sync and backup; the core question content (meta.yaml, prompt, options, etc.) remains independent. If you use the same question folders in another system or without this app, you can ignore or delete db_meta.yaml and still have valid, portable question content.

title: 12  SPEC: Database–Filesystem Question Sync (v0.0.3)
text:
12.1 Goals
This spec describes how question data is kept in sync between the database (source of truth for all application behavior) and the filesystem (mirror/backup). It covers dual-write on create/update, the optional db_meta.yaml file that keeps ownership and status separate from question content, and the sync algorithm when DB and FS disagree.

title: 12  SPEC: Database–Filesystem Question Sync (v0.0.3)
text:
Single source of truth — All listing, “my questions,” tests, and resolution use the database. The filesystem is a mirror for backup and portability.
Dual-write — On every create or update (and on approve), the app writes the same information to the DB and to the FS. Question content stays in meta.yaml and type-specific files; app-only metadata (ownership, status) goes in a separate file so the question content remains portable.
Sync rules — When reconciling FS with DB:

FS-only versions are imported into the DB (under a configured sync owner).
When the same version exists in both and differs, DB wins: the FS copy is moved to a conflicts folder, and the DB version is written to the normal FS path.
DB-only versions can optionally be exported to the FS (e.g. when primary storage is Supabase and an FS backup root is set).

title: 12  SPEC: Database–Filesystem Question Sync (v0.0.3)
text:
12.2 Rationale

Why DB as source of truth? The app needs consistent ownership, approval status, and listing for tests and “my questions.” The database provides a single place for that.
Why keep a filesystem mirror? Backup, recovery, and the ability to use question content outside the app (e.g. in another tool or after a DB failure). The FS layout (one folder per version with meta.yaml, prompt, options) is human-readable and portable.
Why separate db_meta.yaml? So that “just the questions” (meta, prompt, options) stay free of app-specific baggage. You can copy or move question folders and use them elsewhere without ownership/status; the app adds db_meta.yaml only when it needs to sync or mirror that metadata.

title: 12  SPEC: Database–Filesystem Question Sync (v0.0.3)
text:
12.3 Data layout

12.3.1 Question content (portable)

Location: {questions_root}/{logical_id}/{version}/
Files: meta.yaml (id, type, version, title, domain, optional tags, created_at, modified_at), prompt.md or prompt.txt, and type-specific files (e.g. options.yaml). Defined in QUESTION-FORMAT-0.0.1. No ownership or status in these files. For tags, see SPEC-0.0.6.



12.3.2 App metadata (optional)

File: db_meta.yaml in the same version folder.
Fields: owner_id (uuid), status (approved | pending), proposed_by (uuid or null).
Written and read only by this app’s dual-write and sync logic. Can be omitted or deleted when using the folder outside the app.



12.3.3 Conflicts folder

Reserved path: {questions_root}/_conflicts/
When sync resolves a conflict (DB wins), the previous FS version is moved to _conflicts/{logical_id}/{version}_{iso_timestamp}/. That folder keeps the same structure (meta, prompt, options, and any db_meta.yaml). The normal path is then overwritten with the DB version.
List and sync logic exclude _conflicts so those copies are never treated as active questions.

title: 12  SPEC: Database–Filesystem Question Sync (v0.0.3)
text:
12.4 Dual-write behavior
After every successful DB insert or update (create question, new version, upload, approve):

When storage is filesystem
The version folder already exists (written by the store). The app writes or updates only db_meta.yaml in that folder with owner_id, status, proposed_by from the DB row.
When storage is Supabase
If QUESTIONS_FS_BACKUP_ROOT is set, the app writes the full version to that root: all content files (meta, prompt, type-specific) plus db_meta.yaml. So the backup root holds a complete mirror with both content and app metadata.

Dual-write is best-effort: FS write failures do not fail the API request.

title: 12  SPEC: Database–Filesystem Question Sync (v0.0.3)
text:
12.5 Sync algorithm
Sync runs:

At startup: When the server starts, if using filesystem storage, QUESTION_SYNC_OWNER_ID is set, and a Supabase service role key is available (SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY or SERVICE_ROLE_KEY). Runs before any user logs in.
Explicit: Via POST /api/admin/sync-questions (authenticated).

Steps:

List DB — All rows from question_versions (logical_id, version, type, title, domain, owner_id, status, proposed_by, storage_path).
List FS — All (logical_id, version) under the questions root that have a meta.yaml, excluding any path under _conflicts.
FS-only — For each FS version not in the DB: read db_meta.yaml if present; if it has a non-empty owner_id, use that for this version; otherwise use the sync owner (env QUESTION_SYNC_OWNER_ID or the seeded default question owner with fixed UUID). Parse content from FS, insert into DB with that owner_id, status = approved, storage_path = {logical_id}/{version}; then write db_meta.yaml to that version folder.
In both — For each version present in both DB and FS, compare metadata (type, title, domain, owner_id, status, proposed_by). If identical, skip. If different, DB wins: load content from the store (before moving), move the FS version folder to _conflicts/{logical_id}/{version}_{timestamp}, then write the DB version (content + db_meta.yaml) to the normal path.
DB-only (optional) — If desired, export DB-only versions to the FS backup root so the FS eventually mirrors the full DB. (Implementation may do this when backup root is set and primary is Supabase.)

When using the default sync owner (no QUESTION_SYNC_OWNER_ID set), the app uses a single seeded user (fixed UUID). Without running the seed (e.g. hosted Supabase), startup sync is skipped and the UI shows a banner with remediation steps; set QUESTION_SYNC_OWNER_ID to a valid user UUID to enable sync.

text:
12.7 API and listing

GET /api/questions — Lists from the database: latest approved version per logical_id, shape { id, type, version, title, domain }. Sync is run at server startup (see above), not on this request.
POST /api/admin/sync-questions — Runs sync and returns { imported, conflictsResolved, errors }.

All other question operations (get by id, my questions, take test) already use the DB; only sync and content loading read/write the FS.

title: 12  SPEC: Database–Filesystem Question Sync (v0.0.3)
text:
12.8 Summary

DB = source of truth for listing, ownership, and tests.
FS = mirror/backup; question content in meta.yaml + prompt + type-specific files; app metadata in optional db_meta.yaml.
Dual-write = after each DB insert/update, write db_meta.yaml (and when Supabase + backup root, write full version to backup).
Sync = FS-only → import to DB; in both and different → DB wins (FS to _conflicts, then write DB version to FS).

This keeps the question format portable while giving the app a single, consistent place (the database) for ownership and status.

title: 10  SPEC-0.0.1.qmd
text:
10.2 Questions: Storage and database

10.2.1 Rationale
Question content is stored on the filesystem (local dev) or in Supabase Storage (e.g. Vercel). The database (question_versions table) is the source of truth for listing, ownership, status, and which version is “latest.” This allows: - Users to develop and version questions on their own machine (e.g. with Git) when using FS. - The app to have a single source of truth (DB) for who owns what and what is approved. - An optional FS mirror with sync: FS-only versions can be imported into the DB; when both exist and differ, DB wins. See SPEC-DB-FS-QUESTION-SYNC-0.0.3.qmd for dual-write, db_meta.yaml, and sync behaviour.


10.2.2 Layout and metadata

One folder per question version.
See docs/QUESTION-FORMAT-0.0.1.qmd for the canonical folder layout, file names, metadata schema, and all edge cases (e.g. prompt file when both prompt.md and prompt.txt exist, id/type/version validation, type-specific required files, multiple-choice correctness). Implementations MUST follow that document. An optional db_meta.yaml in each version folder stores app metadata (owner_id, status, proposed_by) for sync; question content stays in meta.yaml and type-specific files only.
Required metadata (per question, in meta.yaml and DB):

Unique id (e.g. UUID or slug) — stable across versions.
Question type — e.g. multiple choice, short answer, long answer, R coding, Bash, Excel formula, HTML, CSS (subset as needed for MVP).
Version — so modifications can be tracked and linked to student attempts.

Optional metadata: title, domain, difficulty, rubric reference, etc., as defined in the question format doc.



10.2.3 Question workflow

User creates/edits the question folder and files locally (no need to be connected to the system).
User uploads via the app:

New question: upload a folder (or archive) that conforms to the question format; system assigns or validates id and stores under the configured questions root. Version is approved (owner is the uploader).
Modification to existing question: upload updated files for an existing id; system stores a new version. If the uploader is the question owner, the version is approved; otherwise it is pending until the owner approves it. Only approved versions are used in tests.

System logs when each question was created and when it was last modified (and by whom, if auth provides it).

title: 19  Automated Tests Guide (v0.0.3)
text:
20.1 Overview

Goal: Prevent regression bugs via automated tests. Tests are the primary guardrail when refactoring or when AI agents modify code.
Runner: Vitest (unit and API-level tests). Optional later: Playwright for E2E.
Layout: Colocated unit tests in src/ (e.g. src/lib/questions/version.test.ts). API route tests use mocks for auth and Supabase.
Priority order: (1) Pure lib logic (version, validate, parse, evaluators), (2) API routes with mocks, (3) optional E2E for critical flows.

title: 19  Automated Tests Guide (v0.0.3)
text:
20.3 Test scope and priorities

20.3.1 Phase 1: Unit tests (pure logic)
High-value, no-mock modules under src/lib/:

src/lib/questions/version.ts — parseVersion, isValidVersion, compareVersion, formatVersion, bumpVersion. Cover valid/invalid strings, comparison order, each bump type.
src/lib/questions/validate.ts — validateMetaYaml, validateOptionsYaml, type-specific validators. Use inline fixture objects.
src/lib/questions/parse.ts — parseQuestion, prompt selection. Use in-memory QuestionFile[] arrays.
src/lib/evaluators/short-answer.ts and multiple-choice.ts — evaluateShortAnswer, evaluateMultipleChoice. Cover expected/answers, normalization, correct vs wrong.



20.3.2 Phase 2: API route tests

Call route handlers with constructed NextRequest and params. Mock requireUser and Supabase (e.g. vi.mock("@/lib/auth"), vi.mock("@/lib/supabase/server")).
Assert: invalid input → 400 and stable error shape; unauthenticated → 401 (or your standard); valid input → 200/201 and minimal response fields.
Example routes: POST /api/questions/[id]/versions, GET /api/questions/my, question-set start/submit.



20.3.3 Phase 3: CI and optional E2E

CI: Run npm run test:run and npm run lint on every change; block merge on failure.
E2E (later): Playwright for one or two critical user flows if needed.

title: 19  Automated Tests Guide (v0.0.3)
text:
20.4 Keeping tests robust (anti-fragility)
These rules reduce brittleness and keep the suite useful when refactoring or when AI agents edit code.

20.4.1 Test behavior, not implementation

Assert on inputs and outputs (return values, thrown errors, HTTP status and body). Avoid asserting on internal function call order, exact log messages, or low-level DB query shapes.
Prefer coarse assertions: check the few fields that matter (e.g. status, error, data.id) instead of snapshotting entire responses that change often.



20.4.2 Minimize mocking

Mock only at boundaries: auth and Supabase client. Avoid mocking internal modules or implementation details; that couples tests to refactors.
Unit-test pure functions in src/lib/ without mocks first; add API tests that mock only the external services.



20.4.3 Stable, deterministic tests

No real network, no real time, no unseeded randomness. If time is needed, freeze it in tests.
One failing test should point to one cause: prefer small, single-purpose tests with clear names over long scenario tests that fail in obscure ways.



20.4.4 Fixtures and snapshots

If using fixture files (e.g. YAML), keep them small and purpose-built (one fixture per rule). Avoid large “kitchen sink” fixtures.
Use snapshots sparingly; prefer explicit assertions on a few key fields. If you use snapshots, avoid updating them without reviewing the diff.



20.4.5 Agent-friendly rules (for AI-assisted changes)

Definition of done: Any change that touches behaviour must update or add tests; all tests must pass; no deleting or weakening tests without explicit request.
No silent weakening: Do not remove tests, loosen assertions, or add broad try/catch that hides failures. If a test is wrong, fix or replace it explicitly.
Refactor rule: When refactoring internals, most tests should stay unchanged. If many tests need changes, the tests may be tied to implementation rather than behaviour—prefer fixing tests to assert behaviour.
Invariants as tests: Encode critical invariants (e.g. version sort order, validation error shape, prompt selection) as tests so they act as guardrails against accidental breakage.

Config file: vitest.config.mts at repo root (ESM) so Vitest uses Vite’s ESM API and avoids the CJS deprecation warning. Scripts pass --config vitest.config.mts. Include src/**/*.test.ts and src/**/*.test.tsx; preserve path alias @/* → ./src/*; exclude node_modules and .next.
Placement: Colocated *.test.ts next to the module under test (e.g. version.test.ts beside version.ts).
Scripts: package.json should define "test": "vitest" and "test:run": "vitest run".

title: 8  SPEC 0.0.4 — Implement Bash Questions (v001)
text:
8.1 Two Bash question types
This spec describes the implementation of two Bash question types for yrS3: Type A (write code, auto-check output in a sandbox) and Type B (predict output, no terminal; grading uses runtime-computed expected output). It also extends question sets with optional shared sandbox resources (e.g. a folder tree zip).
References: QUESTION-FORMAT-0.0.1.qmd, QUESTION-MODULE-SPEC.qmd, SPEC-QUESTION-SETS-0.0.2.qmd.

title: 8  SPEC 0.0.4 — Implement Bash Questions (v001)
text:
8.1.1 Type A: Bash (write code, auto-check output)

Goal: The student writes Bash code that produces a required output or behaviour.
Flow: The question can define an optional sandbox folder tree via a zip reference. The student writes Bash in the UI; on submit, the system runs their code in that environment (or a clean env with optional per-test setup commands) and compares stdout to the reference solution’s output.
Grading: Fully automatic: run the reference solution and the student’s code per test case (same stdin/setup), compare stdout.
Question definition: meta.yaml with type: bash; required solution.sh; optional tests.yaml (list of description, stdin, setup); optional sandbox_zip_ref (filename or path to a zip containing the initial folder tree). Individual questions (and each test) can still modify the tree via setup (e.g. touch xyz, mkdir -p a/b/c).



8.1.2 Type B: Bash predict output (bash_predict_output)

Goal: The student predicts what a given Bash script would output, without running anything.
Flow: The question presents only text: the script and any needed context. The student has no terminal; they type their answer. On submit, the system grades their text against the runtime-computed expected output (run the script once, use that as the key).
Grading: The correct answer is not trusted from storage at grading time. The system runs the script in a controlled environment, captures stdout, normalizes it, and compares the student’s normalized answer to that. The question definition does store an expected output (in expected.yaml) for editor review. If the stored expected differs from the computed output, the system uses the computed output for grading and logs an error (e.g. bash_predict_output_stored_expected_mismatch) so maintainers can fix the question.

title: 8  SPEC 0.0.4 — Implement Bash Questions (v001)
text:
8.2 Question definition details

8.2.1 Type A (bash)

Canonical type value: bash.
Required files: meta.yaml, one of prompt.md/prompt.txt, solution.sh.
Optional: tests.yaml (list of test cases with description, stdin, setup). If absent, a single default test with empty stdin is used.
Optional in meta: sandbox_zip_ref — reference to a zip file (e.g. filename in the question version folder, or path) that contains the folder tree for the sandbox. At run time the system extracts this zip to a temp directory and runs the student’s (and reference) script with that directory as the working directory. Per-test setup still runs after the zip is applied, so authors can add or change files.



8.2.2 Type B (bash_predict_output)

Canonical type value: bash_predict_output.
Required files: meta.yaml, one of prompt.md/prompt.txt, script.sh (the script shown to the student), expected.yaml (stored expected output for review; see answer or answers).
Grading: At grading time the system runs script.sh once, normalizes stdout, and compares the student’s normalized answer to that. Stored expected is for display/review only; if it differs from computed, computed wins and a mismatch is logged.

title: 8  SPEC 0.0.4 — Implement Bash Questions (v001)
text:
8.3 Question sets and shared sandbox

Question sets (see SPEC-QUESTION-SETS-0.0.2) are extended with an optional sandbox zip reference so that a set can share a folder tree for all its Bash (Type A) questions.
Set-level field: In set.yaml (file-based) and in the question_sets table (DB): optional sandbox_zip_ref (e.g. filename in the set folder). When present, it can be used as the default sandbox for bash questions in that set that do not define their own sandbox_zip_ref. Resolution of the set’s zip path is implementation-defined (e.g. for file-based sets: path relative to the set folder).
Individual questions in the set can still override with their own sandbox_zip_ref or use only per-test setup with no zip.

title: 8  SPEC 0.0.4 — Implement Bash Questions (v001)
text:
8.4 Sandbox and zip extraction

Sandbox runner: The bash runner supports an optional working directory (cwd). When a question (or set) provides a zip reference, the system extracts that zip to a temporary directory and runs Bash with that directory as cwd.
Zip extraction: Implemented via a small helper (e.g. using the system unzip command) that extracts a given zip path to a temp dir and returns the path. The caller is responsible for cleaning up the temp dir after grading.
Security: Sandbox remains isolated (no network, timeout, limited env). Zip contents are not executed; they only define the filesystem layout for the run.

title: 8  SPEC 0.0.4 — Implement Bash Questions (v001)
text:
8.5 UI

Create question: The “Create question” flow supports a question type selector: Multiple choice, Bash (write code), Bash predict output. The form fields and payload match the chosen type (e.g. solution script + tests + optional sandbox zip ref for Type A; script source + stored expected for Type B).
New version: The “New version” flow supports existing questions of type multiple_choice, bash, and bash_predict_output. The same type-specific forms are used with initial data from the current version.
Take test: For bash, the student gets a code input (and optional “Run” against the sandbox). For bash_predict_output, the student sees the script as text and a textarea for their predicted output (no terminal).

section: 8.8 Developer runbook: get the system running and tested
text:
8.8 Developer runbook: get the system running and tested
This section gives the exact steps a developer needs to run the app and verify the Bash question types. There is no requirement for backward compatibility; the system is not live, so the database can be reset or recreated.

8.8.1 Prerequisites

Node.js 20+ and npm.
Supabase: Either a hosted Supabase project (recommended) or local Supabase (Docker required). For local: Supabase CLI and Docker.
System unzip (for sandbox zip extraction when testing Type A questions with sandbox_zip_ref). On Ubuntu/Debian it is usually present; on macOS install if needed (e.g. via Xcode Command Line Tools or Homebrew).



8.8.2 1. Clone and install
cd /path/to/yrS3
npm install


8.8.3 2. Environment variables
cp .env.example .env.local
Edit .env.local:

NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL — Supabase project URL.
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY — Supabase anon (public) key.

For a hosted project: get these from the Supabase Dashboard → your project → Project Settings → API (Project URL and anon key).
For local Supabase: after starting the stack (step 3), run supabase status -o env and copy the API URL and anon key from the output.
Leave QUESTIONS_STORAGE unset so the app uses the filesystem for questions (recommended for local dev). The repo already includes sample questions under questions/ (including sample-bash-001, sample-bash-002, sample-bash-predict-001, sample-bash-predict-002).
Optional for listing/sync: set QUESTION_SYNC_OWNER_ID to your Supabase user UUID so that FS-only question versions are imported into the DB when the app lists questions. You can add this after signing up (see step 6).


8.8.4 3. Database (migrations)
Option A — Local Supabase (blow away DB and reapply all migrations)
supabase start
supabase db reset
Or use the npm script: npm run db:reset (runs supabase db reset). This applies every migration in supabase/migrations/ and resets the local database. Use this whenever you want a clean schema (e.g. after pulling new migrations).
If the stack was already running and you only changed migrations: supabase db reset is enough. If you changed config.toml or need a clean start: supabase stop --no-backup then supabase start then supabase db reset.
Option B — Hosted Supabase
supabase login
supabase link --project-ref YOUR_PROJECT_REF
supabase db push
This applies migrations to the linked hosted project. To “blow away” the hosted DB you would need to reset or drop objects in the Dashboard (or use a new project); for development, db push is usually enough to add new tables/columns.


8.8.5 4. Start the dev server
npm run dev
Open http://localhost:3000 in a browser.


8.8.6 5. Run automated tests
In a separate terminal, from the repo root:
npm run test:run
All tests (including question validation, parse, serialize, and evaluators for Bash and bash_predict_output) should pass. Use this before committing or to confirm the system after setup.


8.8.7 6. UI flow: sign up and use the app

Sign up / Log in
Go to the app and create an account (email/password). If using local Supabase with email confirmation, open the Mailpit/Inbucket URL from supabase status and use the confirmation link from the captured email.
Question sets
In the UI, open Question sets (or the main navigation that lists sets). You should see any question sets that exist in the DB or on the filesystem (e.g. under question-sets/ if present).
Create a question set (optional)
Click Create question set. Enter a title (e.g. “Bash practice”), optionally a description, and select questions to include. The list comes from the DB (and, when using FS + sync, from the questions/ folder). Select at least the sample Bash questions (e.g. sample-bash-001, sample-bash-predict-001) if they appear, then save. If the sample questions do not appear, ensure they are under questions/<id>/<version>/ with valid meta.yaml and, when using sync, that QUESTION_SYNC_OWNER_ID is set and you have triggered a list (e.g. by visiting the page that lists questions or question sets).
Take as test
From the question sets list, click Take as test (or equivalent) on the set you created. The app starts a test session and shows the first question.
Answer and submit

For multiple choice: choose an option and move to the next (or submit).

For Bash (Type A): type or paste Bash code in the code area; you can click Run to execute it (uses the same sandbox as grading). Move through questions, then click Submit test.

For Bash predict output (Type B): read the script shown, type the output you expect in the text area (no terminal), then move on and Submit test.

View results
After submit, the app shows the score and per-question feedback (e.g. “All tests passed” for Bash, or “Correct.” / “Your answer does not match…” for bash_predict_output).



8.8.8 7. UI flow: create Bash questions (optional)

Go to Create question (or “New question” in the questions area).

In the Question type dropdown, choose Bash (write code — auto-check output) or Bash predict output (explain output, no terminal).

Fill in the form:

Type A (bash): Prompt, reference solution script, optional tests (description, stdin, setup), optional sandbox zip ref.

Type B (bash_predict_output): Prompt, script to show to the student, and stored expected output (for editor review; grading uses the runtime-computed output).


Submit. The question is created and stored (DB + FS when using the app’s create flow). You can then add it to a question set and take a test that includes it.



8.8.9 8. Verify sandbox zip (Type A, optional)
To test a Type A question that uses a zip for the sandbox folder tree: create or use a question whose meta.yaml includes sandbox_zip_ref: somefile.zip, and place somefile.zip in that question’s version folder (e.g. questions/<logical_id>/<version>/somefile.zip). Run a test that includes that question and submit an answer; the grader will extract the zip to a temp dir and run the student and reference scripts with that directory as the working directory. No extra UI steps—just ensure the zip exists and the ref is set.

section: 8.4 Part A: Default question sync owner
text:
8.4 Part A: Default question sync owner

8.4.1 A.1 Current behavior (before implementation)

QUESTION_SYNC_OWNER_ID has no default; when unset, startup sync and FS-only imports are skipped.
FS-only import always uses QUESTION_SYNC_OWNER_ID; db_meta.yaml is not read for ownership on import.
supabase/seed.sql is empty. src/instrumentation.ts and src/lib/questions/sync-questions.ts require the env var. No UI shows sync status or sync errors.



8.4.2 A.2 Design decisions

Use a single seeded user named “default question owner” (not “admin”). The app currently has no concept of an “admin” user or role; the default user’s only purpose is to own FS-imported questions when no owner is set. Do not add admin-only checks or an admin role in this spec. If an admin role is added later, this user can be granted it or a separate admin user can be introduced.
Default owner ID: A fixed UUID defined in one place and reused in seed + app (no runtime lookup).
FS-only import: When importing an FS-only version, read db_meta.yaml; if it has a non-empty owner_id, use it for that version; otherwise use the sync owner (env or default).
Hosted Supabase without seed: When using the default UUID and the env var is not set, verify that a user with that ID exists (e.g. query auth.users) before running startup sync. If the user does not exist, do not run sync; record the skip reason in the sync-status store so the UI shows a prominent banner. Do not rely only on server logs.



8.4.3 A.3 Implementation steps (default sync owner)

8.4.3.1 Step A.3.1 — Define default sync owner constant

Create src/lib/questions/sync-owner.ts.
Export:

DEFAULT_QUESTION_SYNC_OWNER_ID: a single fixed UUID string (e.g. '00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001'). This exact value must be reused in the seed file.
getSyncOwnerId(env?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): returns (env ?? process.env).QUESTION_SYNC_OWNER_ID ?? DEFAULT_QUESTION_SYNC_OWNER_ID so callers get env override when set.

Use this module in both instrumentation and sync-questions so the default is defined in one place only.



8.4.3.2 Step A.3.2 — Seed the default question owner in Supabase

Edit supabase/seed.sql.
Use the exact same UUID as DEFAULT_QUESTION_SYNC_OWNER_ID from the app (import or copy the constant value into the seed so app and seed stay in sync).
auth.users: Enable pgcrypto; hash password with crypt('your-chosen-default-password', gen_salt('bf')). Insert one row with: id = the default UUID, instance_id = '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000', aud = 'authenticated', role = 'authenticated', email = e.g. 'default-question-owner@system.local', encrypted_password = result of crypt, email_confirmed_at = NOW(), raw_app_meta_data = '{"provider":"email","providers":["email"]}', raw_user_meta_data = '{}', created_at / updated_at = NOW().
auth.identities: Insert one row so the user can sign in: id = same UUID, user_id = same UUID, provider = 'email', provider_id = same UUID, identity_data = JSON with sub and email (e.g. format('{"sub": "%s", "email": "default-question-owner@system.local"}', v_user_id)::jsonb), last_sign_in_at, created_at, updated_at = NOW(). Without this row, login will not work in recent Supabase versions.
Reference: Supabase seed auth user pattern.
Document the default email and default password in SETUP or README for local dev login if desired.



8.4.3.3 Step A.3.3 — Sync: use default owner and respect db_meta.yaml owner

Edit src/lib/questions/sync-questions.ts.

For FS-only versions (version not in DB): before calling insertQuestionVersion, call readDbMeta(root, logicalId, version). If the result is non-null and has a non-empty string owner_id, use that owner_id for this version’s insert; otherwise use getSyncOwnerId().
Replace every use of process.env.QUESTION_SYNC_OWNER_ID with either getSyncOwnerId() or the owner chosen from db_meta for that version.
After a successful import, continue to write db_meta.yaml with the owner that was actually used (current behavior).

Do not change the “in both” / conflict logic; DB still wins and writes its version to FS.



8.4.3.4 Step A.3.4 — Instrumentation: run startup sync when default exists

Edit src/instrumentation.ts.

Use only the admin client here: createAdminClient() from src/lib/supabase/admin.ts. Do not use the request-scoped createClient() from server—there is no request at startup.
Use getSyncOwnerId() instead of checking only process.env.QUESTION_SYNC_OWNER_ID. So startup sync is attempted when the env var is set or when the default is used.
Required: When the env var is not set (i.e. using the default UUID), use the admin client to verify that a user with that ID exists (e.g. query auth.users by id). If the user does not exist, do not call syncFsWithDb; instead record in the sync-status store (see Step A.3.5) that sync was skipped with a clear reason (e.g. “Default question owner user not found in database. Run supabase db reset (local) or set QUESTION_SYNC_OWNER_ID.”). Also log to console for dev visibility.
When sync runs, call syncFsWithDb(supabase) (with the admin client), then write the returned SyncResult to the sync-status store (status 'ran', plus imported, conflictsResolved, errors). When sync is skipped, write to the sync-status store (status 'skipped', reason) only.




8.4.3.5 Step A.3.5 — Sync-status store and API

Create src/lib/questions/sync-status.ts.

In-memory store for the last startup or manual sync result. Shape: { status: 'ran' | 'skipped', reason?: string, errors?: string[], imported?: number, conflictsResolved?: number, lastUpdatedAt?: string }.
When sync is skipped: set status: 'skipped' and a clear reason string.
When sync runs: set status: 'ran' and store imported, conflictsResolved, and errors from SyncResult.
Export functions to set and get this state. Both instrumentation and the handler for POST /api/admin/sync-questions must call the setter after running or skipping.

Create src/app/api/sync-status/route.ts (or under src/app/api/admin/sync-status/route.ts).

GET: return the stored sync status as JSON. Response shape: { status: 'ran' | 'skipped', reason?: string, errors?: string[], imported?: number, conflictsResolved?: number, lastUpdatedAt?: string }. When nothing has run yet, return a sensible default (e.g. status 'ran', imported 0, errors []). May be unauthenticated so all users see the banner when there is a problem.
Important: The handler for POST /api/admin/sync-questions must, after calling syncFsWithDb(supabase), write the returned SyncResult into the same sync-status store (set status 'ran', imported, conflictsResolved, errors, lastUpdatedAt) so the UI shows the latest outcome whether from startup or from a manual POST.




8.4.3.6 Step A.3.6 — UI banner for sync status

Add a UI component that fetches GET /api/sync-status and displays a prominent banner when:

status === 'skipped', or
status === 'ran' and errors exists and errors.length > 0.

Banner requirements:

State clearly that the system is running without FS sync having completed successfully (or that sync completed with errors).
Include actionable text for an admin: e.g. “Default question owner not found. To fix: (1) Local: run supabase db reset to create the seed user, or (2) Set QUESTION_SYNC_OWNER_ID to a valid user UUID. Ensure SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY (or SERVICE_ROLE_KEY) is set for startup sync. See SETUP/SPEC-DB-FS-QUESTION-SYNC.”
When errors is non-empty, list the errors or provide an expandable section so admins can see per-version failures (e.g. invalid owner_id in db_meta) without reading log files.
Visually noticeable (e.g. warning style). May be dismissible for the session only.

Integrate this component in the root layout or a shared layout so it appears on all relevant pages.



8.4.3.7 Step A.3.7 — Documentation and env

Edit .env.example: state that QUESTION_SYNC_OWNER_ID is optional when using the seeded default question owner (e.g. after supabase db reset); if set, it overrides the default.
Edit docs/SPEC-DB-FS-QUESTION-SYNC-0.0.3.qmd: update the Configuration table and sync steps to describe the default sync owner (seeded user with fixed UUID), that FS-only import uses db_meta.yaml owner_id when present else sync owner (env or default), and that without seed (e.g. hosted) sync is skipped unless QUESTION_SYNC_OWNER_ID is set.
Edit Setup/README (e.g. docs/SETUP-0.0.1-v001.qmd or README.md): add a short note that for out-of-the-box behavior with FS questions, run supabase db reset and copy supabase status -o env into .env.local; document the default question owner email and default password for local login if desired.




8.4.4 A.4 Edge cases (default sync owner)

db_meta.yaml has invalid or missing user: Insert will fail (FK to auth.users). Keep pushing the error into result.errors; ensure the full sync result (including errors) is written to the sync-status store so the UI banner can show these errors.
Hosted Supabase without seed: The default-user existence check is required; on skip, record status: 'skipped' and a clear reason in the sync-status store so the UI shows the banner with remediation steps.
Existing deployments: If QUESTION_SYNC_OWNER_ID is set, it continues to override the default; no breaking change.



8.4.5 A.5 Sync flow (reference)
flowchart LR
  subgraph startup [Startup]
    A[Instrumentation] --> B{Env QUESTION_SYNC_OWNER_ID set?}
    B -->|Yes| C[Use env UUID]
    B -->|No| D[Use DEFAULT_QUESTION_SYNC_OWNER_ID]
    C --> E{Default UUID? Check user exists}
    D --> E
    E -->|Exists or env set| F[Run syncFsWithDb with admin client]
    E -->|Default and not found| G[Skip sync, write sync-status skipped]
    F --> H[Write sync-status ran + result]
  end
  subgraph import [FS-only import per version]
    F --> I[Read db_meta.yaml]
    I --> J{owner_id present?}
    J -->|Yes| K[Use db_meta.owner_id]
    J -->|No| L[Use getSyncOwnerId]
    K --> M[Insert question_version]
    L --> M
  end

section: 8.5 Part B: System-wide message logging (errors, warnings, info)
text:
8.5 Part B: System-wide message logging (errors, warnings, info)

8.5.1 B.1 Current behavior (before implementation)

src/lib/logger.ts logs only to stdout via console.log; nothing is written to a log file.
API routes and instrumentation catch errors and return generic JSON or log to console; those are not written to a file or pushed to any UI-visible store.
There is no app-wide message store, no error.tsx / global error handler, and no UI that shows recent system messages (errors, warnings, or info).



8.5.2 B.2 Scope and levels

System messages include: errors, warnings, and info (optionally debug). Every such message must be (1) written to a log file and (2) visible in the UI.
Introduce a level for each message: error | warning | info (and optionally debug). If the codebase does not yet distinguish these everywhere, new code should set the appropriate level; existing logs can default to info until updated.
Scope for first version: Server-side only: API route handlers, instrumentation, and uncaught errors handled by Next.js error.tsx. Client-side errors are out of scope unless a separate reporting API is added later.



8.5.3 B.3 Implementation steps (system message logging)

8.5.3.1 Step B.3.1 — Log file and central reporting

Log file: Use a single system log file (e.g. logs/app.log). Path may be configurable via env (e.g. LOG_FILE_PATH). Ensure the log directory exists (create if missing). Append each message as one line. Each line must include a level field (e.g. JSON: { "level": "error" | "warning" | "info", "timestamp": "...", "message": "...", "stack?", "context?", "route?" }). Use a single writer (e.g. fs.appendFile) to avoid concurrent write issues.
Central reporting: Provide a single entry point, e.g. report(level: 'error' | 'warning' | 'info', messageOrError: string | Error, context?: Record<string, unknown>). Implementation may use separate helpers reportError, reportWarning, reportInfo that all call a shared writer. Each call must: (1) write a line to the log file (with level, timestamp, message, and if Error: stack; plus context/route if provided), and (2) append to the in-memory system-message store (see Step B.3.2). Optionally also call the existing stdout logger so current observability is preserved.
Location: Implement in a new file e.g. src/lib/report.ts or src/lib/error-reporting.ts, or extend src/lib/logger.ts. When messageOrError is an Error, use e.message and e.stack for the message and stack fields.



8.5.3.2 Step B.3.2 — System-message store

Create src/lib/system-messages.ts.

In-memory store holding the last N messages (e.g. 50–100). Each entry: { id: string, level: 'error' | 'warning' | 'info', timestamp: string (ISO), message: string, stack?: string, context?: Record<string, unknown>, route?: string }.
Export a function to add a message (and optionally a getter that accepts an optional level filter, e.g. getMessages(level?: 'error' | 'warning' | 'info') returning the list, newest first).
When report(level, messageOrError, context) is called, push to this store (and write to the log file). Same process-only guarantee as sync-status; persisting to DB is an optional follow-up.




8.5.3.3 Step B.3.3 — API for logs

Create src/app/api/logs/route.ts (or src/app/api/errors/route.ts).

GET: return recent messages from the system-message store as JSON.
Query param: level optional; comma-separated list of levels to include, e.g. ?level=error,warning or ?level=error. If omitted, return all levels.
Response shape: { messages: Array<{ id: string, level: 'error' | 'warning' | 'info', timestamp: string, message: string, stack?: string, context?: Record<string, unknown>, route?: string }> }. Newest first. If store is empty, return { messages: [] }.




8.5.3.4 Step B.3.4 — Integration: API routes and instrumentation

In every API route and server path that catches errors and returns 4xx/5xx or logs: before returning the error response, call report('error', e, { route: '<METHOD> <path>' }) (e.g. route: 'GET /api/questions'). Use a consistent route string so the UI can show where the error originated.
API route files that must call report('error', e, { route: ... }) in their catch blocks (as of this spec; add any others that exist or are added later):

src/app/api/questions/route.ts (GET and POST)
src/app/api/questions/[id]/versions/route.ts
src/app/api/questions/upload/route.ts
src/app/api/questions/[id]/versions/[version]/approve/route.ts
src/app/api/admin/sync-questions/route.ts
src/app/api/question-sets/[id]/route.ts
src/app/api/question-sets/route.ts (GET and POST)
src/app/api/questions/pending/route.ts
src/app/api/questions/my/route.ts
Any other route under src/app/api/ that has a catch block and returns an error response (e.g. question-sets submit, run-code, auth callback, signout).

Instrumentation: When startup sync throws or is skipped due to a missing default user, call report('error', error, { source: 'instrumentation' }) (or equivalent) so the error appears in the log file and in the system-message list.
Where the app has or will have warnings or informational messages, call report('warning', message, context) or report('info', message, context) so they too go to the log file and the UI.



8.5.3.5 Step B.3.5 — Next.js error boundary (required)

Create src/app/error.tsx. This is required, not optional. The error boundary must ensure that the error is reported to the server so it is written to the log file and the in-memory system-message store.

If error.tsx runs on the server: Call report('error', error, { source: 'error-boundary' }) directly in the component.
If error.tsx is a Client Component (common in App Router): The report() function and the system-message store live on the server. So the client must send the error to the server, e.g. by calling a new API such as POST /api/report-error with body { message: error.message, stack: error.stack } (or similar). The API route handler then calls report('error', new Error(body.message), { source: 'error-boundary', stack: body.stack }) so the error is logged to the file and added to the store. Implement one of these two approaches so uncaught errors are never only client-side.

Use the standard Next.js App Router error boundary signature (e.g. export default function Error({ error, reset }: { error: Error; reset: () => void })). If the app has a global error handler elsewhere, that handler must also ensure errors are reported (via report() on the server or via the same POST API).



8.5.3.6 Step B.3.6 — UI: system log / messages area

Add a system log / messages UI area (banner, sidebar, or dedicated page) that:

Fetches the logs API (e.g. GET /api/logs with optional ?level=...).
Shows recent messages with color coding by level: e.g. error = red, warning = amber/yellow, info = blue or neutral.
Provides controls: (1) Filter by level — e.g. checkboxes or dropdown: show only errors, errors + warnings, or all levels; (2) Hide/show details — e.g. each row collapsed by default with an expand control to show stack, context, route.
Makes it clear which messages are error vs warning vs info (labels and/or color). If the app does not yet set levels everywhere, default displayed messages to info until call sites are updated.





8.5.4 B.4 Edge cases (system logging)

Log file write failure: Do not throw from report(); best-effort. If file write fails, still push to the in-memory store so the UI shows the message.
Store full: When the store is at capacity (N messages), drop the oldest message when appending a new one.

text:
8.7 Summary

Part A delivers: out-of-the-box FS question import via a seeded default question owner; sync status and sync errors visible in the UI via a prominent banner; FS-only import respects owner_id in db_meta.yaml when present.
Part B delivers: all system messages (errors, warnings, info, debug) logged to a log file and visible in the UI; level-based filtering and color coding; uncaught errors captured via error.tsx and reported to both log file and UI.

title: 8  SPEC: Default question sync owner and system message logging (v0.0.5)
text:
User goal: The system should “work out of the box” without requiring configuration. If there are already question folders on the filesystem (under the questions root) but nothing in the database, the app should import them when the server starts—even before the first user logs in—without the deployer having to set QUESTION_SYNC_OWNER_ID.
Additional goal: Sync outcomes (success, skip, or per-version errors) must be visible in the UI to all users, not only in server logs. An admin who does not know the system should be able to see that FS sync did not run or that specific imports failed, and get actionable steps to fix it (e.g. run seed, set env vars, see SETUP/SPEC).



User goal: Every system message (errors, warnings, info, debug) must be (1) written to a log file and (2) visible in the UI. No one should have to find or tail log files to see what went wrong or what the system reported. This is especially important during development and for admins who need to diagnose issues.
Additional goal: The UI should support filtering by level (error / warning / info / debug), color coding by level, and hiding/showing details (stack, context, route). Uncaught errors (e.g. in React rendering) must also be captured via Next.js error.tsx and reported to both the log file and the UI.

text:
8.2 Relevant existing code (do not reimplement)

Sync: src/lib/questions/sync-questions.ts — syncFsWithDb(supabase) returns SyncResult { imported: number, conflictsResolved: number, errors: string[] }. Use this; do not reimplement sync logic.
DB meta on FS: src/lib/questions/db-meta-fs.ts — readDbMeta(root, logicalId, version) returns { owner_id, status, proposed_by } | null. Use it to read owner_id for FS-only import. The file lives at {QUESTIONS_ROOT}/{logical_id}/{version}/db_meta.yaml.
Admin Supabase client: src/lib/supabase/admin.ts — createAdminClient() returns a Supabase client using the service role key (env: SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY or SERVICE_ROLE_KEY). Use this in instrumentation only, because startup runs before any request and there are no cookies; the normal server createClient() is request-scoped and cannot be used at startup.

section: 8.5 Part B: System-wide message logging (errors, warnings, info, debug)
text:
8.5 Part B: System-wide message logging (errors, warnings, info, debug)

8.5.1 B.1 Current behavior (before implementation)

src/lib/logger.ts logs only to stdout via console.log; nothing is written to a log file.
API routes and instrumentation catch errors and return generic JSON or log to console; those are not written to a file or pushed to any UI-visible store.
There is no app-wide message store, no error.tsx / global error handler, and no UI that shows recent system messages (errors, warnings, info, or debug).



8.5.2 B.2 Scope and levels

System messages include: errors, warnings, info, and debug. Every such message must be (1) written to a log file and (2) visible in the UI.
Introduce a level for each message: error | warning | info | debug. If the codebase does not yet distinguish these everywhere, new code should set the appropriate level; existing logs can default to info until updated.
Scope for first version: Server-side only: API route handlers, instrumentation, and uncaught errors handled by Next.js error.tsx. Client-side errors are out of scope unless a separate reporting API is added later.



8.5.3 B.3 Implementation steps (system message logging)

8.5.3.1 Step B.3.1 — Log file and central reporting

Log file: Use a single system log file (e.g. logs/app.log). Path may be configurable via env (e.g. LOG_FILE_PATH). Ensure the log directory exists (create if missing). Append each message as one line. Each line must include a level field (e.g. JSON: { "level": "error" | "warning" | "info" | "debug", "timestamp": "...", "message": "...", "stack?", "context?", "route?" }). Use a single writer (e.g. fs.appendFile) to avoid concurrent write issues.
Central reporting: Provide a single entry point, e.g. report(level: 'error' | 'warning' | 'info' | 'debug', messageOrError: string | Error, context?: Record<string, unknown>). Implementation may use separate helpers reportError, reportWarning, reportInfo, reportDebug that all call a shared writer. Each call must: (1) write a line to the log file (with level, timestamp, message, and if Error: stack; plus context/route if provided), and (2) append to the in-memory system-message store (see Step B.3.2). Optionally also call the existing stdout logger so current observability is preserved.
Location: Implement in a new file e.g. src/lib/report.ts or src/lib/error-reporting.ts, or extend src/lib/logger.ts. When messageOrError is an Error, use e.message and e.stack for the message and stack fields.



8.5.3.2 Step B.3.2 — System-message store

Create src/lib/system-messages.ts.

In-memory store holding the last N messages (configurable via SYSTEM_MESSAGE_STORE_SIZE, default 1000). Each entry: { id: string, level: 'error' | 'warning' | 'info' | 'debug', timestamp: string (ISO), message: string, stack?: string, context?: Record<string, unknown>, route?: string }.
When full, drop oldest when appending. When the user requests older messages (e.g. “Load older” on the /logs page), load from the log file in batches (configurable via SYSTEM_MESSAGE_LOAD_OLDER_BATCH, default 100) and expand the in-memory store (do not remove newest messages).
Export a function to add a message and a getter with optional level filter; export getOlderMessages(olderThanId, levelFilter?) that reads the log file and returns the next batch of older messages, merging them into the store.
When report(level, messageOrError, context) is called, push to this store (and write to the log file with id in each line so older messages can be loaded). Same process-only guarantee as sync-status; persisting to DB is an optional follow-up.




8.5.3.3 Step B.3.3 — API for logs

Create src/app/api/logs/route.ts (or src/app/api/errors/route.ts).

GET: return recent messages from the system-message store as JSON.
Query param: level optional; comma-separated list of levels to include, e.g. ?level=error,warning or ?level=error. If omitted, return all levels.
Response shape: { messages: Array<{ id: string, level: 'error' | 'warning' | 'info' | 'debug', timestamp: string, message: string, stack?: string, context?: Record<string, unknown>, route?: string }> }. Newest first. If store is empty, return { messages: [] }.




8.5.3.4 Step B.3.4 — Integration: API routes and instrumentation

In every API route and server path that catches errors and returns 4xx/5xx or logs: before returning the error response, call report('error', e, { route: '<METHOD> <path>' }) (e.g. route: 'GET /api/questions'). Use a consistent route string so the UI can show where the error originated.
API route files that must call report('error', e, { route: ... }) in their catch blocks (as of this spec; add any others that exist or are added later):

src/app/api/questions/route.ts (GET and POST)
src/app/api/questions/[id]/versions/route.ts
src/app/api/questions/upload/route.ts
src/app/api/questions/[id]/versions/[version]/approve/route.ts
src/app/api/admin/sync-questions/route.ts
src/app/api/question-sets/[id]/route.ts
src/app/api/question-sets/route.ts (GET and POST)
src/app/api/questions/pending/route.ts
src/app/api/questions/my/route.ts
Any other route under src/app/api/ that has a catch block and returns an error response (e.g. question-sets submit, run-code, auth callback, signout).

Instrumentation: When startup sync throws or is skipped due to a missing default user, call report('error', error, { source: 'instrumentation' }) (or equivalent) so the error appears in the log file and in the system-message list.
Where the app has or will have warnings, informational messages, or debug output, call report('warning', message, context), report('info', message, context), or report('debug', message, context) so they too go to the log file and the UI.



8.5.3.5 Step B.3.5 — Next.js error boundary (required)

Create src/app/error.tsx. This is required, not optional. The error boundary must ensure that the error is reported to the server so it is written to the log file and the in-memory system-message store.

If error.tsx runs on the server: Call report('error', error, { source: 'error-boundary' }) directly in the component.
If error.tsx is a Client Component (common in App Router): The report() function and the system-message store live on the server. So the client must send the error to the server, e.g. by calling a new API such as POST /api/report-error with body { message: error.message, stack: error.stack } (or similar). The API route handler then calls report('error', new Error(body.message), { source: 'error-boundary', stack: body.stack }) so the error is logged to the file and added to the store. Implement one of these two approaches so uncaught errors are never only client-side.

Use the standard Next.js App Router error boundary signature (e.g. export default function Error({ error, reset }: { error: Error; reset: () => void })). If the app has a global error handler elsewhere, that handler must also ensure errors are reported (via report() on the server or via the same POST API).



8.5.3.6 Step B.3.6 — UI: system log / messages area

Add a system log / messages UI area (banner, sidebar, or dedicated page) that:

Fetches the logs API (e.g. GET /api/logs with optional ?level=...).
Shows recent messages with color coding by level: e.g. error = red, warning = amber/yellow, info = blue or neutral, debug = gray or muted.
Provides controls: (1) Filter by level — e.g. checkboxes or dropdown: show only errors, errors + warnings, all levels, or include/exclude debug; (2) Hide/show details — e.g. each row collapsed by default with an expand control to show stack, context, route.
Makes it clear which messages are error vs warning vs info vs debug (labels and/or color). If the app does not yet set levels everywhere, default displayed messages to info until call sites are updated.





8.5.4 B.4 Edge cases (system logging)

Log file write failure: Do not throw from report(); best-effort. If file write fails, still push to the in-memory store so the UI shows the message.
Store full: When the store is at capacity (N messages), drop the oldest message when appending a new one.

10.1 Purpose and goals
This spec defines a tag system for questions and a questions browser UI. Questions may have multiple tags. Tags are stored and indexed in the database and stored in the filesystem version of each question. When creating a question set, users can filter available questions by tags. A new “Browse questions” page allows any authenticated user to see all approved questions (not only those they own). This document is written so that an implementer (or an LLM) can implement it without access to prior discussion.
Part A — Tag system
Part B — Questions browser

title: 10  SPEC: Question tags and questions browser (v0.0.6)
text:
User goal: Authors and instructors can attach tags to questions (e.g. bash, intro, week-2) so that questions can be filtered and discovered by topic or category.
Storage: Tags are part of question content: stored in meta.yaml in each version folder and in the database (question_versions.tags) for indexing and filtering. Sync and dual-write keep FS and DB in sync; tags are ingested from the filesystem when reading the FS question store into the DB.
Filtering: When creating a question set, the user can filter the list of available questions by one or more tags (questions that have all selected tags are shown). The same filter is available in the questions browser.



User goal: Today the only way to see questions is to create a question set (picker list) or take a test. Users need a dedicated way to browse all questions—to see what exists, search or filter by tags, and view metadata (id, title, type, domain, tags) without building a set or taking a test.
Scope: The browser shows all approved questions (any owner), one row per logical_id (latest version). Optional tag filter. No ownership filter; everyone sees the same catalog.

10.3 Part A: Tag system

10.3.1 A.1 Data model
Filesystem (meta.yaml)

Add optional field tags: array of non-empty strings, e.g. tags: [bash, intro, week-1]. Omitted or empty means no tags. Order is not significant; duplicates should be normalized away on read/write.

Database

Add column tags to question_versions: type text[], default '{}'. Create a GIN index for containment queries: create index idx_question_versions_tags on question_versions using gin(tags);. Filtering “questions that have all of [tag1, tag2]” uses tags @> array['tag1','tag2'] (Supabase: .contains('tags', ['tag1','tag2'])).

Types (TypeScript)

MetaYaml, ParsedQuestion, QuestionMetaListItem: add optional tags?: string[].
QuestionVersionRow, InsertQuestionVersion: add tags: string[] | null (or string[] with default).
Payload types used for create/update (e.g. BashPayload, MultipleChoicePayload, BashPredictOutputPayload): add optional tags?: string[] so new questions can set tags.



10.3.2 A.2 Parse and serialize

parse.ts: When loading meta.yaml, set question.tags from meta.tags: if present and array, map to non-empty strings and dedupe; otherwise undefined.
serialize.ts: In every path that builds meta (serializeMultipleChoice, serializeBash, serializeBashPredictOutput, serializeParsedQuestion), add if (payload.tags?.length) meta.tags = payload.tags (or question.tags for serializeParsedQuestion) so that tags are written to meta.yaml when present.



10.3.3 A.3 Validation

validate.ts (validateMetaYaml): Allow optional tags; if present, must be an array of strings; normalize to non-empty strings in returned meta. Invalid entries (non-strings) can be dropped or rejected per project convention; recommend accept array and filter to strings.



10.3.4 A.4 Sync and ingestion

sync-questions.ts: When building the insert payload for an FS-only version, include tags: question.tags ?? []. When comparing FS vs DB for “in both” case, include tags in the comparison (sameMeta); if tags differ, DB wins and we overwrite FS with DB version (serializeParsedQuestion already writes tags when present). After insert, writeDbMeta is unchanged (tags live in meta.yaml, not db_meta.yaml).
insertQuestionVersion: Accept and insert tags (array or empty array).
dual-write / writeQuestionVersionToFs: No change; content files (including meta.yaml with tags) come from serialize; db_meta.yaml stays owner/status only.



10.3.5 A.5 API and listing

GET /api/questions: Accept optional query param tags (e.g. ?tags=bash,intro or multiple tags=bash&tags=intro). Parse to string[]. Call a listing function that returns approved latest-per-logical_id, with optional filter: when tags provided, only rows where tags contains all of them. Include tags in each returned item: { id, type, version, title, domain, tags }.
DB layer: Add (or extend) a function e.g. listApprovedQuestionsForListing(supabase, { tags?: string[] }) that returns the same shape as the current list (latest approved per logical_id), applying .contains('tags', tags) when tags are provided. Implement “latest per logical_id” in application code after the query if needed (filter by status, then dedupe by logical_id taking latest by version).

10.5 Part C: Backfill tags on existing questions (filesystem)

Goal: Existing question version folders may have no tags in meta.yaml. To avoid empty tags everywhere and to make filtering useful, backfill tags once on the filesystem.
Approach: One-time script (e.g. scripts/backfill-question-tags.ts or .mts) that:

Iterates every version directory under the questions root (use listVersionKeysFromFs and read each version’s meta.yaml).
For each meta.yaml, if tags is missing or empty, derive tags from existing fields: e.g. [domain, type].filter(Boolean) deduped, normalized (e.g. lowercase, trim). Optionally include a slug from title if desired.
Writes back meta.yaml with the new tags field (preserve other keys and formatting as much as possible).

After backfill: Run sync (or rely on next startup sync) so the database is updated from FS. No separate DB-only backfill required; sync will populate tags from the updated meta.yaml.
