text:
9.1 Purpose and scope
This spec defines the design and storage approach for hierarchical tags (to disambiguate terminology across domains and organize content) and canonical facts (to map questions and tutorial content via a shared database of normalized facts). It also specifies minimal tutorial content storage and AI-assisted duplicate detection for tags and facts. The system must support filesystem persistence for tags and facts so that editors and content creators can work in the filesystem or via the UI (see PRD-0.0.1-v003.qmd system goals). Design targets scalability on the order of millions of facts and tens of thousands of tags (not “Google” scale, but internet-scale growth).
References: SPEC-0.0.6-QUESTION-TAGS-AND-BROWSE.qmd, QUESTION-FORMAT-0.0.1.qmd, PRD-0.0.1-v003.qmd, SPEC-DB-FS-QUESTION-SYNC-0.0.3.qmd, DOC-GUIDE-v001.qmd.
crumbs: 9  SPEC: Hierarchical tags and canonical facts (v0.0.8)

title: 9  SPEC: Hierarchical tags and canonical facts (v0.0.8)
text:
9.1.1 Goals

Hierarchical tags: Allow the same term to mean different things in different contexts (e.g. “if” in Python vs Bash). Support organization and discovery of questions and tutorial content by scoped tags (e.g. programming/python/if). Persist tags on the filesystem and in the database.
Canonical facts: Maintain a single normalized representation of each fact so that tutorial content and questions can be linked to the same fact regardless of wording. Support “this question requires these facts” (prerequisites) and “this tutorial teaches these facts” (coverage). Persist facts on the filesystem and in the database.
Tutorial content (minimal): Support minimal tutorial content entities that can be stored in several ways (direct content, pointer only, pointer + full copy, pointer + excerpt) and linked to facts and tags.
Duplicate reduction: Use AI-assisted workflows so that when new tags or facts are proposed (or facts modified), potential duplicates are surfaced and the human editor must converse with the AI before proceeding; overrides are logged for administrator review; merge functionality preserves full history.



9.1.2 Scope of this spec

In scope: Data model and storage for hierarchical tags and canonical facts; filesystem layout and sync for both; scalability considerations; choice of tag path separator; AI-assisted duplicate detection and merge workflow; minimal tutorial content storage modes; link tables for questions and tutorials; UI preference for search over raw IDs.
Out of scope: Full tutorial authoring workflows; extraction of facts from free text (assume facts are created/curated); detailed AI prompt design for duplicate detection (only the workflow and storage of conversations are specified).



9.1.3 Backwards compatibility
There is no requirement for backwards compatibility. The system has not gone live; flat tags from SPEC-0.0.6 can be replaced by hierarchical tag references (tag IDs or stable path strings). Migration of existing data is a one-time implementation task.

title: 9  SPEC: Hierarchical tags and canonical facts (v0.0.8)
text:
9.3 Hierarchical tags

9.3.1 Problem
Many domains reuse the same terminology (e.g. “if” in Python vs Bash; “call” in finance vs telephony). A hierarchical tag system supports disambiguation and a consistent way to refer to scoped concepts (e.g. “if in the Python language”).


9.3.2 Tag path separator
Two options were considered:









Separator
Example
Pros
Cons




/
programming/python/if, python/control-flow
Standard for hierarchical paths (URLs, taxonomies); allows hyphen in segment names (e.g. control-flow).
Could be confused with filesystem paths in documentation—but the logical path is independent of how tags are stored on disk.


-
python-if, python-control-flow
No slash/directory confusion.
Ambiguous: is python-control-flow two segments or one? Hard to extend to deeper hierarchy (e.g. programming-python-control-flow-if is unwieldy).



Recommendation: use / as the path separator. It is the conventional choice for hierarchies, allows hyphens inside segment names (programming/python/control-flow), and scales to arbitrary depth. How tags are stored on the filesystem (e.g. in directories or in a single file) is an implementation detail and should not dictate the logical separator.
Convention: Path format is domain/subdomain/.../term (e.g. programming/python/if, programming/html/elements/paired). A small set of top-level domains (e.g. programming, finance, telephony) helps avoid proliferation of equivalent paths.


9.3.3 Storage options









Approach
Description
Pros
Cons




Adjacency list
Table with id, name, parent_id (self-referential).
Simple; cheap inserts and moves; works well with recursive CTEs in Postgres.
Descendant/ancestor queries need recursion (CTE).


Materialized path
Store full path as string or array (e.g. programming/python/if).
Fast prefix matching; good for display and filter-by-path.
Can be derived from adjacency list or stored redundantly.


Closure table
Separate table (ancestor, descendant, depth).
Very fast ancestor/descendant queries.
More rows; more complex writes.



Recommendation: Use adjacency list as primary storage; store or compute a normalized path (with /) for display and prefix filtering. Index the path (or path prefix) for scalable filter queries. Treat the taxonomy as curated (admin/maintainer-defined) so path conventions stay consistent.


9.3.4 Filesystem persistence for tags
Tags must be persistable on the filesystem so that editors can create and edit them outside the UI (see system goals in PRD-0.0.1-v003.qmd).

Layout: Define a tags root (e.g. tags/). Options: (a) one file per tag (e.g. tags/{path-with-slashes-replaced}.yaml or a directory tree tags/programming/python/if.yaml), or (b) a single or few YAML files that list the taxonomy (e.g. tags/taxonomy.yaml with a tree structure). The exact layout is an implementation choice; the spec requires that tags can be read from and written to the filesystem and synced with the database (same dual-write/sync philosophy as questions in SPEC-DB-FS-QUESTION-SYNC-0.0.3.qmd).
Sync: Database remains source of truth for listing and filtering; filesystem is a mirror. FS-only tags can be imported; conflict resolution (DB wins vs FS wins) should follow the same pattern as question sync. Tag references on questions (and tutorials) are stored as tag IDs or stable path strings; when syncing from FS, path strings can be resolved to tag IDs using the taxonomy.



9.3.5 Relation to existing flat tags
Replace flat tags: string[] (SPEC-0.0.6) with hierarchical tag references only: store tag IDs or stable path strings (e.g. programming/python/if) on questions. No backwards compatibility; migrate existing flat tag values to the new taxonomy as part of implementation.


9.3.6 Use cases

Organize and filter questions and tutorial content by hierarchical tag or path.
Support “map question to tutorials” by shared tag path.
Scope facts by domain (tag path) for filtering.

title: 9  SPEC: Hierarchical tags and canonical facts (v0.0.8)
text:
9.4 Canonical facts

9.4.1 Purpose
A single fact can be expressed in many ways. A canonical fact is one normalized representation, stored once. Tutorial content and questions link to it by ID; a future process (manual or AI) can match free text to fact IDs.
Example canonical statements:

“In HTML, a ‘container or paired’ element must start with a <start> tag and end with a </end> tag (same name).”
“In HTML the ‘h1’ element is a paired element.”
“In HTML, the ‘h1’ element is used to delineate a 1st level heading.”



9.4.2 Storage approach
Facts table

id: Stable identifier (e.g. UUID).
canonical_text: The fact in normalized form (required).
tag_path (optional): For organization and filtering (e.g. programming/html).
created_at / updated_at: Timestamps.

Indexes: on tag_path (or domain), and full-text or search index on canonical_text for scalable search (see UI section below).
Structured fields (optional): subject, predicate, object
For a minimal knowledge-graph style, facts can optionally store a triple (subject, predicate, object) in addition to or instead of free-form canonical_text. This supports:

Structured querying: e.g. “all facts where subject = ‘h1 element’ and predicate = ‘is a’”.
Consistency: Same predicate vocabulary (e.g. “is a”, “used for”, “requires”) across facts.
Interop: Export or reason over facts as a small graph.

Examples of structured representation:









canonical_text (human-readable)
subject
predicate
object




In HTML, the ‘h1’ element is a paired element.
HTML h1 element
is a
paired element


In HTML, the ‘h1’ element is used to delineate a 1st level heading.
HTML h1 element
used to delineate
1st level heading


In HTML, the ‘table’ element is a paired element.
HTML table element
is a
paired element


In HTML, a paired element must start with an opening tag and end with a closing tag with the same name.
HTML paired element
must have
opening and closing tag with same name



The system may store both canonical_text (for display and full-text search) and optional (subject, predicate, object) (for structured filter or graph use). If only one form is stored, canonical_text is the minimum. Implementation can add subject, predicate, object columns or a separate table; the spec does not mandate the schema for the optional triple.
Link tables (many-to-many)

question_prerequisite_facts(question_version_id, fact_id): This question requires understanding this fact.
question_facts(question_version_id, fact_id): Optional; this question exercises or reinforces this fact.
tutorial_facts(tutorial_id, fact_id): This tutorial (or segment) teaches this fact. (See minimal tutorial content below.)

Filesystem persistence for facts
Facts must be persistable on the filesystem so that editors can create and edit them outside the UI.

Layout: Define a facts root (e.g. facts/). Options: (a) one file per fact (e.g. facts/{uuid}.yaml or by path facts/programming/html/h1-paired.yaml), or (b) one or more YAML files listing facts (e.g. facts/index.yaml with an array or map). Each fact file (or entry) must include at least id, canonical_text, and optional tag_path, timestamps.
Sync: Database is source of truth for listing and linking; filesystem is a mirror. FS-only facts can be imported; conflicts resolved per the same pattern as question sync.

text:
9.2 Scalability
Design for:

Facts: Potentially millions of rows (e.g. 1M–10M+). Use indexes on canonical_text (or full-text search), tag_path/domain, and any foreign keys. Consider partitioning by domain or tag_path for query and maintenance at scale; full-text search infrastructure (e.g. Postgres tsvector or external search) should support millions of documents.
Tags: Potentially tens of thousands of nodes (e.g. 10k–50k+). Adjacency list with indexed parent_id and optional materialized path; recursive CTEs are acceptable at this scale. Index path or path prefix for filter-by-path queries; ensure hierarchy traversal remains efficient.
Link tables (question–fact, tutorial–fact, etc.): Row counts will be very large (questions × facts per question, etc.). Index by content id and by fact_id for both directions of lookup. Design for millions of link rows; consider partitioning or sharding if a single table grows beyond comfortable range.

title: 9  SPEC: Hierarchical tags and canonical facts (v0.0.8)
text:
9.5 Minimal tutorial content
This version implements minimal tutorial content: a tutorial is a linkable entity that can reference external or internal content and can be tagged and linked to facts. Four storage modes are supported:

Direct content only: Tutorial content is stored entirely in the system—e.g. text, images, Word documents, or other files. No external pointer. Use case: original content authored and held only in yrS3.
Pointer only: Store only a pointer to external content (e.g. URL, ISBN/title/page/paragraph, reference to an academic paper). The system does not store the content itself. Use case: reference to a live web page or a book; no backup or excerpt in yrS3.
Pointer + full document: Store the pointer and a full copy of the source document in yrS3 (for backup and historical preservation). Use case: external source may disappear; we preserve a snapshot.
Pointer + excerpt: Store the pointer and only the excerpt from the document that contains the relevant fact (or more context). Use case: cite a specific passage; avoid storing the entire document while keeping the cited portion in yrS3.

Implementation must support these four modes (e.g. tutorial record has: optional external reference, optional stored content type [full document vs excerpt], optional binary or text content). Tutorials can be linked to facts (teaches) and to hierarchical tags. Tutorial content is persistable on the filesystem in line with system goals; exact layout (e.g. tutorials/{id}/meta.yaml plus optional content.* or excerpt.*) is an implementation detail.

title: 9  SPEC: Hierarchical tags and canonical facts (v0.0.8)
text:
9.6 AI-assisted duplicate detection and merge

9.6.1 Goals

Reduce duplicate tags (e.g. “programming/python/if” vs “python/control-statements/if” or similar).
Reduce duplicate or near-duplicate canonical facts when adding or modifying facts.
Human has final say; AI supports the decision and logs overrides for administrator review.



9.6.2 Workflow (tags and facts)
When a user proposes a new tag (or a new fact, or a modification to an existing fact):

Search: The system (using AI and/or full-text/similarity search) searches existing tags (or facts). If one or more potential duplicates are found, the user is not allowed to proceed without a conversation.
Conversation: The human must converse with the AI about the merits of adding the new tag (or fact) vs using an existing one. The AI presents the potential duplicate(s) and reasoning; the human may argue for a new tag (e.g. different meaning, different scope). The AI may rebut. This exchange continues until the human makes a decision.
Decision: The human decides: (a) use an existing tag/fact (abandon or merge), or (b) create the new tag/fact anyway.
Override logging: If the AI has flagged a likely duplicate and the human nevertheless creates the new tag/fact (override), the system allows the action but:

Logs the event for an administrator (e.g. in a dedicated table or log store).
Stores the AI summary of why it considered this a duplicate, and the human’s rebuttal (the human is shown the AI’s complaints and is asked to provide a response).
The full conversation (AI and human messages) is stored in the filesystem and/or database so that an administrator can review the full exchange.
The human is informed that this override will be logged and that an administrator may review it.


If no potential duplicate is found, the user may create the tag/fact without this workflow (normal create path).


9.6.3 Merge
When duplicates are identified (e.g. by an admin or by the same AI-assisted flow):

Merge functionality: The system must support merging two (or more) tags into one, and two (or more) facts into one. All references (questions, tutorials, link tables) are updated to point to the surviving tag/fact.
History: The entire history of the merge (which tag/fact was merged into which, when, by whom) must be stored and recoverable. Merged-away tags/facts are retained in a “merged” or historical state so that old references can be resolved and audits are possible (soft delete or history table).

Storage for conversations and override logs may be in the database, the filesystem, or both; the spec requires that the data be persistable and reviewable by an administrator.

title: 9  SPEC: Hierarchical tags and canonical facts (v0.0.8)
text:
9.7 UI: search over IDs
All UIs that involve tags or facts should favor natural language and search over raw IDs:

Search for a tag: At minimum, provide a full-text or path-prefix search over tag names and paths. The user types (e.g. “python if” or “programming/python”) and sees matching tags; selection is by click or choose from list, not by typing a UUID.
Search for a fact: At minimum, provide full-text search over canonical_text (and optional subject/predicate/object). The user types a phrase and sees matching facts; selection by click or choose from list. Additional filters (e.g. by tag path, by subject) may be added for power users.

Users should not be required to memorize or paste UUIDs or internal IDs when attaching tags or facts to questions or tutorials.

9.7.1 Tag filter bar (implementation)
The tag filter bar (e.g. on the Browse questions and Create set pages) loads the list of available tags as follows:

Primary source: GET /api/tags — returns the hierarchical tag taxonomy (array of objects with path, or array of path strings). The UI displays these so the user can filter by tag path without typing UUIDs.
Fallback: If the taxonomy is unavailable — e.g. the response is not OK (404, 500), the response body is not valid JSON (e.g. an HTML error page), or the parsed JSON is not a recognized array shape — the bar falls back to GET /api/questions/tags, which returns the distinct tag values currently used on questions (flat strings). This ensures the filter still works when the taxonomy API is missing or failing.
Failure: If both requests fail or return unusable data, the bar shows an empty list. See src/app/components/tag-filter-bar-load.ts and tag-filter-bar-load.test.ts for the logic and tests.

title: 8  SPEC: AI duplicate UI, override logging, tag merge, tutorial sync (v0.0.9)
text:
8.1 Purpose and scope
This spec implements the deferred items from SPEC-0.0.8-HIERARCHICAL-TAGS-AND-CANONICAL-FACTS.qmd: (1) AI duplicate-detection conversation UI, (2) override logging on create, (3) merge for tags (in addition to the existing facts merge), and (4) tutorial sync from filesystem on startup. The database schema and APIs for tags, facts, tutorials, override_logs, and merge_logs already exist from v0.0.8; this spec defines the missing flows, UI, and sync behavior.
References: SPEC-0.0.8-HIERARCHICAL-TAGS-AND-CANONICAL-FACTS.qmd, TAGS-FORMAT-0.0.8.qmd, FACTS-FORMAT-0.0.8.qmd, DOC-GUIDE-v001.qmd.

title: 8  SPEC: AI duplicate UI, override logging, tag merge, tutorial sync (v0.0.9)
text:
8.1.1 Goals

Duplicate-detection UI: When a user proposes a new tag or fact (or edits a fact), run a duplicate check; if potential duplicates are found, require a conversation with the AI before the user can proceed. The UI must support this flow and store the conversation and any override in the database.
Override logging on create: When the user overrides the AI (creates the tag/fact anyway despite a duplicate warning), write an entry to override_logs (entity_type, entity_id, ai_summary, human_rebuttal, conversation_json, created_by) at create time—not only have the schema and a list API.
Tag merge: Provide a merge API for tags (analogous to the existing merge API for facts): choose a surviving tag and a merged tag; update all references (question_versions.tags, tutorial_tag_paths, and any other consumers) from the merged path to the surviving path; remove or retire the merged tag; record the merge in merge_logs.
Tutorial sync from FS: On startup (and optionally via an admin sync endpoint), sync tutorials from the filesystem into the database: import FS-only tutorials, resolve conflicts with DB-wins semantics, and optionally write the DB state back to the FS mirror. Use the same dual-source pattern as questions and question sets.



8.1.2 Scope

In scope: Duplicate-check API and conversation/override flow for tags and facts; UI for the conversation and override confirmation; persistence of override_logs on create; tag merge API and path-update logic; tutorial sync (FS → DB, conflict resolution, startup and admin trigger).
Out of scope: Detailed AI prompt design; extraction of facts from free text; full tutorial authoring workflows.

section: 8.2 Part A: AI duplicate-detection and override logging
text:
8.2 Part A: AI duplicate-detection and override logging

8.2.1 A.1 Duplicate check (backend)

Tags: When the user proposes a new tag (path and optionally name), the system must search existing tags for potential duplicates. Criteria may include: path equality, path similarity (e.g. same leaf segment, same prefix), or semantic similarity (e.g. via an AI or embedding step). Return a list of candidate duplicate tags (id, path, name) and, if using AI, a short reason (e.g. “Same path segment ‘if’ under a similar parent”).
Facts: When the user proposes a new fact (canonical_text) or an edit to an existing fact, the system must search existing facts for potential duplicates. Use at least: full-text or substring match on canonical_text. Optionally use AI or embeddings for near-duplicate detection. Return candidate facts (id, canonical_text, tag_path) and an optional reason.
API: Provide endpoints that the create/edit UI can call before submitting the create/update, e.g.:

POST /api/tags/check-duplicates — body: { path, name? }; response: { candidates: Array<{ id, path, name, reason? }>, is_duplicate: boolean }.
POST /api/facts/check-duplicates — body: { canonical_text, exclude_id? }; response: { candidates: Array<{ id, canonical_text, tag_path, reason? }>, is_duplicate: boolean }.

If candidates.length > 0, the UI must not allow a direct create/update; it must enter the conversation flow (see below). If the user then chooses to create anyway, the create API must record an override (see A.3).



8.2.2 A.2 Conversation flow (UI)

When the duplicate check returns one or more candidates:

Show the candidate(s) and the AI’s reason (if any) in the UI.
Start a conversation: The user can send messages (e.g. “I need a separate tag for X because …”); the system sends the user message and current context (new tag/fact, candidates) to an AI and returns the AI’s reply. This may be a single exchange or multiple turns. The UI must support at least one user message and one AI reply; multiple turns are recommended.
Decide: The user chooses one of:

Use existing: Abandon the create (or link to an existing tag/fact). No new entity is created; no override log.
Create anyway (override): Proceed with create. The system allows the create and logs an override (A.3). The user must be informed that this action will be logged for administrator review and must be given a chance to provide a rebuttal (short text) that is stored with the override.


Storage: The full conversation (ordered list of { role: ‘user’ | ‘assistant’, content: string }) must be stored. Store it in the override_logs.conversation_json column when an override occurs. Optionally persist the conversation in a separate table or in the filesystem for non-override cases (e.g. when the user later chooses “use existing”); the minimum is to persist when the user overrides.



8.2.3 A.3 Override logging on create

When the user creates a tag or fact after the duplicate-check flow and chooses “create anyway”:

Create the tag or fact as normal (insert into tags or facts).
Insert a row into override_logs with:

entity_type: 'tag' or 'fact'.
entity_id: the new tag or fact id (uuid).
ai_summary: text summarizing why the AI considered this a duplicate (from the duplicate-check or conversation).
human_rebuttal: the rebuttal text provided by the user (optional but encouraged).
conversation_json: JSON array of the conversation messages (role, content).
created_by: the authenticated user id.

Do not block or roll back the create; the override is recorded for administrator review (existing GET /api/admin/override-logs can list these).

The same applies when the user updates a fact and the duplicate check returns candidates and the user overrides: log to override_logs with entity_id = the fact id being updated.



8.2.4 A.4 UI requirements (summary)

Tag create UI: call duplicate check before submit; if candidates, show conversation flow; on “create anyway,” collect rebuttal, then submit create and ensure backend writes override_logs.
Fact create/edit UI: same pattern—duplicate check, conversation, optional rebuttal, then create/update and override log when the user overrides.
Users must be able to search tags and facts by text/path (no need to type UUIDs); duplicate-check and conversation are in addition to existing search.

title: 8  SPEC: AI duplicate UI, override logging, tag merge, tutorial sync (v0.0.9)
text:
8.3 Part B: Tag merge

8.3.1 B.1 Behavior

Merge tag A into tag B: Tag B is the surviving tag (path and row remain). Tag A is the merged tag (path and row will be removed or retired).
References: Questions and tutorials reference tags by path (e.g. question_versions.tags is text[] of paths; tutorial_tag_paths has tag_path). Therefore:

Replace every occurrence of the merged path (tag A’s path) with the surviving path (tag B’s path) in:

question_versions.tags (array update: replace element merged_path with surviving_path where present).
tutorial_tag_paths.tag_path (update rows where tag_path = merged_path to tag_path = surviving_path; if this creates a duplicate row for the same tutorial_id, collapse to one).

Delete the merged tag row from tags (tag A). If the taxonomy must retain history, alternatively soft-delete (e.g. add a merged_into_id or deleted_at column) and leave the row; this spec allows either, but at least one of delete or soft-delete is required.
Insert into merge_logs: entity_type = 'tag', surviving_id = tag B’s id, merged_id = tag A’s id, merged_by = authenticated user.

Idempotency: If the merged tag path no longer appears in any table (e.g. already updated), the merge can still proceed (delete tag row and write merge_logs).



8.3.2 B.2 API

POST /api/admin/merge/tags — body: { surviving_id: uuid, merged_id: uuid }. Validates that both ids exist in tags and that surviving_id ≠ merged_id. Performs path replacement in question_versions and tutorial_tag_paths, then deletes the merged tag and inserts into merge_logs. Returns { ok: true, surviving_id, merged_id } or an error.



8.3.3 B.3 Edge cases

If the surviving tag row is missing or the merged tag row is missing, return 400.
If replacing the path in question_versions.tags or tutorial_tag_paths would create a duplicate (e.g. tutorial already has both paths), replace the merged path with the surviving path and ensure a single row per (tutorial_id, surviving_path); for question_versions, ensure the tags array has no duplicate path entries after replacement.

section: 8.4 Part C: Tutorial sync from filesystem
text:
8.4 Part C: Tutorial sync from filesystem

8.4.1 C.1 Scope

Source: Tutorials root (e.g. TUTORIALS_ROOT or tutorials/). Layout per SPEC-0.0.8 and tutorial store-fs: one folder per tutorial {id}/, with meta.yaml (id, title, external_ref, content_mode, stored_content_path, fact_ids, tag_paths, timestamps).
Target: Database tables tutorials, tutorial_facts, tutorial_tag_paths. DB is the source of truth for listing and for in-app behavior; the FS is a mirror for authoring and portability.



8.4.2 C.2 Sync semantics

FS-only tutorial: A folder under the tutorials root with a valid meta.yaml and an id that does not exist in tutorials → import: insert into tutorials, then insert into tutorial_facts and tutorial_tag_paths from meta.yaml. Use the id from the file as the primary key (so that FS and DB ids match).
In both FS and DB: If the same tutorial id exists in both, compare core fields (e.g. title, external_ref, content_mode, stored_content_path). If different, DB wins: overwrite the FS copy with the DB version (write meta.yaml and any stored content paths from DB), or move the FS version to a conflicts folder and write the DB version to the normal path—same pattern as question sync in SPEC-DB-FS-QUESTION-SYNC-0.0.3.qmd. If same, skip.
DB-only tutorial: Optionally, export tutorials that exist only in the DB to the FS (e.g. for backup). Minimum required: support FS → DB import and conflict resolution (DB wins).



8.4.3 C.3 When sync runs

On startup: When the app starts (e.g. in the same place where question and question-set sync runs), run tutorial sync after questions and question sets (and tags/facts): scan the tutorials root, import FS-only tutorials, resolve conflicts (DB wins), and optionally write back the DB state to the FS for synced tutorials.
Admin trigger: Extend the existing admin sync endpoint (e.g. POST /api/admin/sync-questions or a dedicated POST /api/admin/sync) to run tutorial sync as well, and return counts (e.g. tutorialsImported, tutorialsConflictsResolved).



8.4.4 C.4 Implementation notes

Reuse the existing listTutorialIdsFromFs, readTutorialFromFs (or equivalent) to read from FS. For each id, if not in DB, insert; if in DB, compare and apply DB-wins rule. Writing back to FS: use existing or new helpers to write meta.yaml (and optionally content) from the DB row plus tutorial_facts and tutorial_tag_paths.
Conflicts folder: if using one (e.g. tutorials/_conflicts/{id}_{timestamp}/), exclude it from the list of tutorial ids when scanning.

section: 8.5 Part D: Implementation order and checklist
text:
8.5 Part D: Implementation order and checklist

8.5.1 Recommended order

Override logging on create — Ensure that when a tag or fact is created (or a fact updated) and the duplicate-check flow was shown and the user chose “create anyway,” the backend that performs the create/update also inserts into override_logs. This may require adding an optional body field (e.g. override_reason, conversation, ai_summary) to POST /api/tags and POST /api/facts (and PATCH /api/facts) so the UI can pass the rebuttal and conversation when overriding.
Duplicate-check APIs — Implement POST /api/tags/check-duplicates and POST /api/facts/check-duplicates (and optionally include an AI step that returns a reason). Use simple path/text matching first; add AI or embeddings later if desired.
Conversation UI — Build the UI flow for tag and fact create (and fact edit): call check-duplicates; if candidates, show conversation (user message → AI reply, at least one round); offer “use existing” vs “create anyway”; if “create anyway,” collect rebuttal and send create with override payload so the backend can write override_logs.
Tag merge API — Implement POST /api/admin/merge/tags with path replacement in question_versions and tutorial_tag_paths, delete merged tag, insert merge_logs.
Tutorial sync — Implement syncTutorialsFromFs (or equivalent): list FS tutorial ids, for each FS-only insert into DB and optionally write back; for each in both compare and apply DB-wins; wire sync into startup and into the admin sync endpoint.



8.5.2 Checklist (summary)







Item
Description




Override on create
Backend writes to override_logs when user creates tag/fact (or updates fact) after choosing “create anyway” in duplicate flow; store ai_summary, human_rebuttal, conversation_json, created_by.


Duplicate-check APIs
POST /api/tags/check-duplicates and POST /api/facts/check-duplicates; return candidates and optional reason.


Conversation UI
Tag/fact create (and fact edit) UI: show candidates, run conversation, “use existing” or “create anyway” with rebuttal.


Tag merge API
POST /api/admin/merge/tags; update question_versions.tags and tutorial_tag_paths; delete merged tag; insert merge_logs.


Tutorial sync
Sync tutorials from FS on startup and via admin sync; FS-only import; DB wins on conflict; optional FS write-back.
